features.name: Register File
features.description:
# Register File (F_REG_FILE)

The Register File is the foundational register infrastructure component that implements the complete set of memory-mapped control and status registers defined in the SD Host Controller specification. It provides the hardware interface for software to configure command generation, manage data transfers, control power states, and monitor controller status through standardized register offsets (0x000h through 0x3Fh). This feature encompasses all standard registers including Command, Transfer Mode, Block Size/Count, Response, Present State, Host Control, Power Control, and interrupt management registers that enable full programmability of SD/SDIO/MMC protocol operations.

features.name: Register Access Types
features.description:
# Register Access Types (F_REG_ACCESS_TYPES)

**Purpose:**
This feature defines the access mechanisms and protocols for reading and writing to SD Host Controller registers, establishing whether registers support read-only (RO), write-only (WO), or read-write (RW) operations. It ensures proper register interaction patterns and prevents invalid access attempts that could corrupt controller state or data transfers.

**Behavior:**
The feature categorizes all registers in the host controller's register map (as defined in section 2.1) with specific access type attributes, allowing software drivers to understand which registers can be safely read for status information, which can be written for configuration, and which support both operations. This access control is fundamental to the register infrastructure, preventing firmware from attempting incompatible operations on registers like the Response Register (read-only) or Command Register (write-only), thereby maintaining data integrity and proper command sequencing.

features.name: Register Initial Values
features.description:
# Register Initial Values (F_REG_INIT_VALUES)

This feature defines the power-on and reset default values for all SD Host Controller registers, ensuring predictable and safe initialization states across different implementations. It establishes baseline configurations for control registers, status registers, and interrupt masks that allow firmware to reliably detect the controller's capabilities and operational state without requiring prior configuration. By specifying these initial values (as detailed in section 2.1.3), the feature guarantees interoperability and prevents undefined behavior during controller startup and reset sequences.

features.name: Reserved Bits Handling
features.description:
# Reserved Bits Handling (F_REG_RESERVED_BITS)

This feature defines the proper handling and behavior of reserved bits within SD Host Controller registers as specified in section 2.1.4 of the specification. Reserved bits must be treated as read-only and typically return zero when read, while writes to these bits are ignored to ensure forward compatibility and prevent unintended side effects on register functionality. Proper reserved bit handling is critical for maintaining register integrity across different hardware implementations and software versions, allowing the specification to evolve without breaking existing controller designs.

features.name: Command Engine
features.description:
# Command Engine (F_CMD_ENGINE)

The Command Engine is the core execution unit of the SD Host Controller responsible for generating and managing SD command sequences to the card. It orchestrates command transmission by processing the Command Register (Offset 00Eh) and Argument 1 Register (Offset 008h) to construct properly formatted SD commands, while monitoring command completion through the Response Register (Offset 010h) and Present State Register (Offset 024h). This feature works in conjunction with the Transfer Mode Register to coordinate data transfers and handles command-specific operations including Auto CMD12 support for automatic command termination in multi-block transfers.

features.name: Command Issuance
features.description:
# Command Issuance (F_CMD_ISSUANCE)

Command Issuance is the core mechanism by which the SD Host Controller initiates SD commands to the card by writing command parameters and control information to the Command Register (offset 00Eh) and related registers. This feature orchestrates the setup and transmission of SD commands, including argument configuration via the Argument 1 Register, transfer mode specification via the Transfer Mode Register, and command type/index selection, ultimately triggering the command state machine to execute the command on the SD bus.

The feature handles the complete command pipeline from software configuration through hardware execution, ensuring proper sequencing of command setup registers before the actual command issuance trigger, and managing the interaction with other command engine components like response capture and interrupt signaling upon command completion.

features.name: Command Finalization
features.description:
# Command Finalization (F_CMD_FINALIZATION)

Command Finalization handles the completion and status resolution of SD commands issued by the host controller. This feature manages command response collection, error detection, and the transition of command state machines to idle after command execution completes. It ensures proper handling of command completion interrupts and status flags (such as Command Complete and Command Timeout Error) as defined in the interrupt control and present state registers.

features.name: Command Inhibit
features.description:
# Command Inhibit (F_CMD_INHIBIT)

Command Inhibit is a control mechanism that prevents the SD Host Controller from issuing new commands to the SD card when certain conditions are active. This feature monitors and enforces command execution restrictions by checking inhibit flags in the Present State Register (offset 024h) before allowing command writes to the Command Register (offset 00Eh). It ensures proper sequencing of command operations by blocking command issuance during data transfers, when the command line is busy, or when the controller is in specific operational states like suspend mode.

features.name: Response Handling
features.description:
# Response Handling (F_RESPONSE)

**Purpose:**
Response Handling manages the capture, storage, and interpretation of SD card responses to issued commands within the SD Host Controller's command engine. This feature processes response data from the SD card and makes it available to the host software through the Response Register (Offset 010h).

**Behavior:**
The feature automatically captures response frames returned by the SD card following command transmission, handling variable response types (R1, R1b, R2, R3, R4, R5, R5b, R6, R7) with different lengths and formats. It stores the response data in the Response Register and generates appropriate interrupt signals to notify the host software when responses are available or when response-related errors occur (CRC errors, timeout, etc.).

**Technical Context:**
As a child of the Command Engine (F_CMD_ENGINE), Response Handling works in conjunction with command generation and DMA operations to complete the command-response transaction cycle, with timing and state management coordinated through the Present State Register and interrupt control mechanisms.

features.name: Data Transfer
features.description:
# Data Transfer Feature

The Data Transfer feature enables the SD Host Controller to manage the movement of data between the host system and SD cards through configurable block-based transfers. It orchestrates data flow using registers such as the Block Size Register, Block Count Register, and Transfer Mode Register, while supporting multiple transfer mechanisms including SDMA (Simple DMA), ADMA2 (Advanced DMA), and programmed I/O via the Buffer Data Port. The feature handles critical aspects including buffer pointer control, block length determination, large data segmentation, and interrupt-driven completion signaling to ensure reliable and efficient data exchange across various SD card operations.

features.name: Buffer Data Port
features.description:
# Buffer Data Port (F_BUFFER)

The Buffer Data Port is a 32-bit register (offset 0x20h) that provides the primary data transfer interface between the SD Host Controller and the host system for PIO (Programmed I/O) mode operations. It enables direct read/write access to the controller's internal buffer, allowing the host to manually transfer data to/from SD cards when DMA is not utilized or for small data transfers.

This register operates in conjunction with buffer control mechanisms (sections 1.7.1-1.7.3) that manage buffer pointer advancement and block length determination, supporting both single and multi-block data transfers through sequential port accesses.

features.name: Programmed I/O
features.description:
# Programmed I/O (PIO) Feature

Programmed I/O enables data transfer between the SD Host Controller and the SD card through software-controlled, register-based access via the Buffer Data Port Register (Offset 020h), eliminating the need for DMA hardware. The host driver manually reads from or writes to this register in software loops, with the controller managing the data flow state and signaling completion through interrupt flags. This method provides a simpler, lower-performance alternative to DMA for scenarios where minimal latency or hardware complexity is preferred, particularly for small data transfers or systems without DMA support.

features.name: Single DMA
features.description:
# Single DMA (SDMA) Feature

Single DMA (SDMA) is a basic DMA mechanism that enables the SD Host Controller to transfer data directly between the SD card and system memory without CPU intervention, using a single contiguous memory buffer. The controller automatically manages data movement through the SDMA System Address register (offset 0x00), which points to the host system memory location, while the Block Size and Block Count registers define the transfer parameters. This feature simplifies data transfers for standard SD operations by handling block-by-block DMA operations with automatic address incrementation, reducing CPU overhead compared to PIO-based transfers.

features.name: Advanced DMA 2
features.description:
# Advanced DMA 2 (ADMA2) Feature

Advanced DMA 2 is a sophisticated direct memory access mechanism that enables efficient data transfers between SD cards and system memory using descriptor-based table-driven operations. Unlike simple DMA, ADMA2 uses a descriptor table to specify multiple data segments, their memory addresses, and lengths, allowing the controller to autonomously execute complex multi-block transfers with minimal CPU intervention. This feature significantly improves data throughput and reduces latency by eliminating the need for software to manage individual block transfers, making it essential for high-performance SD Host Controller implementations.

features.name: ADMA2 Descriptor Table
features.description:
# ADMA2 Descriptor Table (F_ADMA2_DESC)

The ADMA2 Descriptor Table is a memory-resident data structure that defines a sequence of DMA transfer operations for the Advanced DMA2 (ADMA2) engine in an SD Host Controller. Each descriptor entry specifies the physical address and length of a data buffer segment, along with control attributes (valid, end-of-table, interrupt flags) that govern how the ADMA2 controller processes the transfer. The host driver constructs this table to enable efficient, scatter-gather DMA transfers without requiring the controller to pause between multiple data blocks, significantly reducing CPU overhead during large SD card data operations.

features.name: ADMA2 State Machine
features.description:
# ADMA2 State Machine (F_ADMA2_STATES)

The ADMA2 State Machine manages the operational states and transitions of the Advanced DMA2 engine within the SD Host Controller, orchestrating the execution of descriptor-based data transfers. It controls the progression through states such as Idle, Fetch, Execute, and Transfer Complete, ensuring proper sequencing of descriptor table parsing, address generation, and data movement operations. This state machine is critical for autonomous DMA operation, allowing the controller to process multiple descriptors without CPU intervention while maintaining data integrity and handling error conditions.

features.name: Block Size and Count
features.description:
# Block Size and Count Feature

The Block Size and Count feature controls the fundamental parameters of SD data transfers by configuring the block size (via the Block Size Register at offset 004h) and the number of blocks to transfer (via the Block Count Register at offset 006h). These registers work in conjunction with the Transfer Mode Register to define the total data payload size and enable the host controller to properly segment large transfers into manageable block-sized chunks for DMA or PIO operations. This feature is essential for supporting variable block lengths and multi-block transfers, allowing the host to efficiently handle diverse SD card data operations while maintaining proper buffer management and interrupt signaling.

features.name: Large Data Transfer Division
features.description:
# Large Data Transfer Division (F_LARGE_DATA_DIV)

**Purpose:**
This feature enables the SD Host Controller to divide large data transfers that exceed single-operation limits into multiple manageable blocks or DMA transactions. It manages the segmentation of data payloads according to buffer constraints and block count register limitations.

**Behavior:**
The controller automatically partitions oversized transfers using the Block Size Register (offset 004h) and Block Count Register (offset 006h) to determine appropriate chunk sizes, while coordinating with the Buffer Control mechanism (section 1.7.3) to handle pointer advancement and block boundary management. This division strategy is particularly critical for SDMA and ADMA2 operations, ensuring compliance with data address and length requirements (section 1.13.3) while maintaining proper interrupt signaling and suspend/resume capability across transaction boundaries.

features.name: Auto CMD Mechanism
features.description:
# Auto CMD Mechanism (F_AUTO_CMD)

The Auto CMD Mechanism automatically generates and issues CMD12 (Stop Transmission) or CMD23 (Set Block Count) commands without requiring explicit software intervention, reducing command overhead during multi-block data transfers. This feature is controlled via the Transfer Mode Register and works in conjunction with the Block Count Register to seamlessly terminate data operations or pre-specify block counts, improving SD Host Controller efficiency and reducing latency in block-oriented transactions.

features.name: Auto CMD12
features.description:
# Auto CMD12 Feature Description

Auto CMD12 automatically generates and issues a STOP_TRANSMISSION (CMD12) command at the completion of a multi-block data transfer, eliminating the need for software to manually send CMD12. This feature is controlled via the Transfer Mode Register and significantly simplifies the command sequence for block read/write operations by reducing software overhead.

When enabled, the SD Host Controller monitors the block count and automatically terminates the data transfer with CMD12 once all blocks have been transmitted or received, improving efficiency in multi-block transactions.

features.name: Auto CMD23
features.description:
# Auto CMD23 Feature Description

Auto CMD23 automatically generates and issues CMD23 (SET_BLOCK_COUNT) commands to the SD card prior to multi-block read/write operations, eliminating the need for software to manually send this command. This feature is part of the Auto CMD command generation capability and works in conjunction with the Transfer Mode Register to enable seamless block count specification for reliable multi-block data transfers. When enabled, the host controller uses the Block Count Register value to automatically construct and transmit CMD23 before executing the actual data transfer command, streamlining the command sequence and reducing software overhead.

features.name: Interrupt System
features.description:
# Interrupt System (F_INTERRUPT)

The Interrupt System feature manages event signaling and status notification in the SD Host Controller through dedicated interrupt control registers that flag various operational conditions such as command completion, data transfer events, and error conditions. This system enables the host driver to respond asynchronously to controller state changes without continuous polling, improving system efficiency and responsiveness. The interrupt mechanism works in conjunction with the register map (particularly interrupt status and enable registers) to allow selective masking of events and prioritized handling of critical conditions like command timeouts, CRC errors, and DMA completion.

features.name: Normal Interrupt Status
features.description:
# Normal Interrupt Status Feature

The Normal Interrupt Status register reports the occurrence of non-error interrupt events within the SD Host Controller, such as command completion, transfer completion, buffer ready conditions, and card insertion/removal events. This register provides a real-time status bitmap that allows the host driver to identify which normal operations have completed and require servicing. Each bit in this register corresponds to a specific normal interrupt source, and bits are typically cleared by writing a '1' to the respective bit position, enabling interrupt-driven operation of the SD Host Controller.

features.name: Error Interrupt Status
features.description:
# Error Interrupt Status Feature

The Error Interrupt Status register captures and reports various error conditions that occur during SD Host Controller operations, including command timeout, CRC errors, end-bit errors, and index errors. This register serves as a status indicator that allows the host driver to identify which specific error condition triggered an interrupt, enabling appropriate error handling and recovery procedures. When an error occurs, the corresponding bit in this register is set and can trigger an interrupt signal to the processor if the corresponding error interrupt enable bit is configured in the interrupt control registers.

features.name: Interrupt Status Enable
features.description:
# Interrupt Status Enable Feature

The Interrupt Status Enable feature controls which interrupt events are permitted to generate actual interrupt signals to the host system by enabling or disabling specific interrupt sources at the controller level. When an interrupt status bit is enabled in this register, the corresponding interrupt condition will propagate to the interrupt output; when disabled, the interrupt event is still detected and logged in the Interrupt Status register but does not trigger an interrupt signal. This feature is essential for selective interrupt masking, allowing software to configure which SD Host Controller events (such as command completion, data transfer completion, errors, or card insertion/removal) should actively interrupt the processor.

features.name: Interrupt Signal Enable
features.description:
# Interrupt Signal Enable Feature

The Interrupt Signal Enable feature controls whether detected interrupt conditions within the SD Host Controller are actually propagated as signal interrupts to the host system. When enabled, interrupt events (such as command completion, data transfer completion, or error conditions) trigger an active interrupt signal; when disabled, the interrupt status is still recorded in interrupt status registers but does not generate an interrupt signal. This feature is essential for managing interrupt-driven operation modes and allows the host software to selectively enable/disable interrupt signaling while maintaining visibility into controller status through register polling.

features.name: Auto CMD Error Status
features.description:
# Auto CMD Error Status Feature

The Auto CMD Error Status feature captures and reports errors that occur during automatic CMD12 (Stop Transmission) command execution in the SD Host Controller. When Auto CMD12 is enabled for multi-block transfers, this feature monitors the command execution and sets specific error status bits in an interrupt register if the automatic stop command fails (e.g., due to command timeout, CRC errors, or index errors). The host driver can then read these error status bits to diagnose why the automatic command termination failed and take appropriate recovery actions.

features.name: Clock System
features.description:
# Clock System (F_CLOCK)

The Clock System feature manages the generation and control of the SD clock (SDCLK) signal that synchronizes all SD card communication within the host controller. This feature includes clock frequency selection, enabling/disabling the clock output, and clock stability monitoring to ensure proper timing for SD command and data transfers. It interfaces with the clock control registers (detailed in section 1.12: Controlling SDCLK) to allow software to configure clock dividers and manage power-efficient clock gating while maintaining compliance with SD specification timing requirements.

features.name: Internal Clock and SDCLK Supply
features.description:
# Internal Clock and SDCLK Supply (F_CLK_SUPPLY)

This feature manages the generation and distribution of the internal clock and SDCLK (SD card clock) signals within the SD Host Controller. It provides clock frequency division and gating mechanisms to supply the SD card interface with the appropriate clock frequency, typically controlled through the Clock Control Register (referenced in section 1.12: Controlling SDCLK). The internal clock must be stable and properly configured before SDCLK is enabled to the SD card, ensuring reliable command and data transfer operations.

features.name: Clock Stop Mechanism
features.description:
# Clock Stop Mechanism (F_CLK_STOP)

The Clock Stop Mechanism enables the SD Host Controller to halt the SDCLK output to the SD card while maintaining the controller's operational state, primarily for power management and suspend/resume operations. This feature allows software to stop the clock via control registers (as detailed in section 1.12: Controlling SDCLK) without disrupting command or data transfer sequences, supporting the power state transitions defined in section 1.10. The mechanism works in conjunction with the Suspend and Resume Mechanism (section 1.6) to enable efficient power consumption during idle periods or when the SD card requires clock gating.

features.name: Clock Frequency Change
features.description:
# Clock Frequency Change Feature

The Clock Frequency Change feature enables the SD Host Controller to dynamically adjust the SDCLK frequency during operation by modifying the clock divider settings in the Clock Control Register (as detailed in section 1.12: Controlling SDCLK). This allows the host to support different SD card speed modes (identification, default, high-speed, etc.) and adapt to varying bus conditions without requiring a full controller reset.

The feature operates by allowing software to change the clock division factor while managing the clock enable/disable state, ensuring proper synchronization and preventing data corruption during frequency transitions. This is essential for SD protocol compliance, which mandates specific clock frequencies for different operational phases and card capabilities.

features.name: Dual Clock Domain
features.description:
# Dual Clock Domain Feature

The Dual Clock Domain feature enables the SD Host Controller to operate with two independent clock domains—typically a slower host interface clock and a faster SD card clock (SDCLK)—allowing asynchronous communication between the controller and the SD card. This architecture isolates clock domains to prevent metastability issues and enables flexible clock frequency management, where the SDCLK can be independently controlled and tuned (as referenced in section 1.12 and 1.16) without affecting the host system's clock domain. The dual clock domain design is essential for supporting variable SD card speeds and implementing sampling clock tuning mechanisms while maintaining stable operation across different voltage and frequency conditions.

features.name: Sampling Clock Tuning
features.description:
# Sampling Clock Tuning Feature

**Purpose:** Sampling Clock Tuning enables dynamic adjustment of the SD clock sampling phase to optimize data reception timing across varying operating conditions and speed modes (SDR, DDR, HS200, etc.). This feature compensates for signal propagation delays and timing skew that can degrade data integrity at higher clock frequencies.

**Behavior:** The host controller implements a tuning mechanism that adjusts the sampling clock delay relative to the SD clock, allowing the controller to find the optimal phase window for reliable data capture. This is typically performed during speed mode transitions or when signal quality degrades, with tuning parameters stored in dedicated control registers (detailed in section 1.16) to maintain optimal timing across different operating conditions.

features.name: Power Control
features.description:
# Power Control (F_POWER)

The Power Control feature manages the SD card power supply states and voltage regulation within the SD Host Controller, enabling software to enable/disable power delivery and select appropriate voltage levels (3.3V, 3.0V, or 1.8V) for different SD card types and operating modes. This feature is critical for power management, card initialization, and supporting voltage switching sequences required by modern SD specifications. It interfaces with the Power Control Register (Offset 029h) to control power state transitions as defined in section 1.10 (Power State Definition of SD Host Controller).

features.name: Bus Power and Voltage Select
features.description:
# Bus Power and Voltage Select Feature

This feature enables the SD Host Controller to manage power delivery to the SD card and select the appropriate voltage level for operation. It controls the power supply enable/disable state and voltage rail selection (typically 3.3V, 3.0V, or 1.8V) through the Power Control Register (Offset 029h), allowing the host to safely power up the card and negotiate voltage compatibility during initialization. The feature is essential for proper card detection, enumeration, and voltage switching sequences required by the SD specification.

features.name: Power States D0-D3
features.description:
# Power States D0-D3 Feature

The Power States D0-D3 feature defines the SD Host Controller's power management states, enabling dynamic power consumption control through multiple operational and low-power modes. This feature allows the host controller to transition between active states (D0) and progressively deeper sleep states (D1, D2, D3) to optimize power efficiency while maintaining the ability to resume SD card communication. The power state transitions are controlled via the Power Control Register (Offset 029h) and related power management mechanisms, enabling software to manage the controller's power envelope based on system requirements and SD card activity levels.

features.name: 1.8V Signaling Enable
features.description:
# 1.8V Signaling Enable (F_1V8_SIGNALING)

This feature enables the SD Host Controller to operate at 1.8V signaling levels, supporting high-speed SD modes (SDR104, DDR50) that require reduced voltage operation compared to the standard 3.3V. The host controller manages voltage switching through the Power Control Register (offset 0x29h) and related power state definitions (section 1.10), allowing dynamic transitions between 3.3V and 1.8V signaling to optimize performance and power consumption during speed mode transitions.

features.name: Bus Width Control
features.description:
# Bus Width Control (F_BUS_WIDTH)

The Bus Width Control feature enables the SD Host Controller to configure the data bus width for SD card communication, typically supporting 1-bit, 4-bit, or 8-bit modes as defined in the SD specification. This control is managed through the Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) and directly impacts data transfer throughput by determining how many data lines are active during read/write operations. By allowing software to dynamically adjust bus width, this feature optimizes performance based on card capabilities and application requirements while maintaining backward compatibility with legacy single-bit mode devices.

features.name: Speed Mode Support
features.description:
# Speed Mode Support (F_SPEED_MODES)

Speed Mode Support enables the SD Host Controller to operate at multiple clock frequencies and signal voltage levels, allowing it to dynamically switch between SD speed modes (Default Speed, High Speed, SDR12, SDR25, SDR50, SDR104, DDR50, etc.) based on card capability negotiation. This feature is controlled through the Host Control 1 Register (offset 028h) and related clock control mechanisms (section 1.12) that manage SDCLK frequency and UHS mode selection. The controller uses sampling clock tuning (section 1.16) to ensure reliable data transfer at higher speeds by optimizing the timing relationship between the clock and data signals.

features.name: Default Speed Mode
features.description:
# Default Speed Mode (F_DEFAULT_SPEED)

The Default Speed Mode is the baseline operating mode of an SD Host Controller that operates at the standard SD clock frequency (up to 25 MHz), providing compatibility with legacy SD cards and devices. This mode is configured through the Host Control 1 Register (Offset 028h) and serves as the fallback speed when higher-speed modes (High Speed, SDR, DDR) are either not supported by the connected card or explicitly disabled. Default Speed Mode ensures reliable data transfer for standard SD protocol compliance while consuming minimal power compared to advanced speed modes.

features.name: High Speed Mode
features.description:
# High Speed Mode (F_HIGH_SPEED)

High Speed Mode enables the SD Host Controller to operate at elevated clock frequencies (up to 52 MHz) compared to Default Speed mode, significantly increasing data transfer throughput for compatible SD cards. This mode is configured through the Host Control 1 Register and requires proper SDCLK frequency management as defined in section 1.12, allowing the controller to support faster command and data transfer rates while maintaining protocol compliance. When enabled, the controller adjusts timing parameters and signal integrity to reliably communicate at these higher speeds with SD devices that support the High Speed capability.

features.name: UHS-I SDR50
features.description:
# UHS-I SDR50 Speed Mode

UHS-I SDR50 is an Ultra High Speed bus mode that enables the SD Host Controller to operate at 50 MHz clock frequency with single data rate (SDR) signaling, providing up to 50 MB/s throughput. This mode requires proper clock tuning via the sampling clock mechanism (section 1.16) and configuration through the Host Control 1 Register to select the appropriate UHS speed mode. The controller must support voltage switching and timing adjustments to maintain signal integrity at this higher speed compared to standard High-Speed mode.

features.name: UHS-I SDR104
features.description:
# UHS-I SDR104 Feature Description

UHS-I SDR104 is an Ultra High Speed (UHS) operating mode that enables the SD Host Controller to communicate with compatible SD cards at a maximum clock frequency of 208 MHz in single data rate (SDR) configuration. This mode requires proper clock tuning via the sampling clock tuning mechanism (section 1.16) to maintain signal integrity at these elevated speeds and is controlled through the Host Control 1 Register settings for UHS mode selection. SDR104 represents the highest performance speed mode within the UHS-I specification, delivering significantly faster data transfer rates compared to standard High Speed modes.

features.name: UHS-I DDR50
features.description:
# UHS-I DDR50 Speed Mode

UHS-I DDR50 is an Ultra High Speed bus mode that enables double data rate (DDR) operation at 50 MHz, allowing the SD Host Controller to achieve 100 MB/s throughput by capturing data on both rising and falling clock edges. This mode requires proper clock tuning (as defined in section 1.16) and configuration of the Host Control 1 Register (section 2.2.10) to set the appropriate UHS speed mode bits and enable DDR signaling. The controller must support the electrical and timing requirements for this higher-speed mode while maintaining backward compatibility with legacy SD devices.

features.name: Card Detection
features.description:
# Card Detection Feature

Card Detection enables the SD Host Controller to identify the physical presence or absence of an SD card in a slot by monitoring card insertion and removal events. This feature typically uses a dedicated card detect pin that signals slot occupancy status, which is reflected in the Present State Register (Offset 024h) and can trigger interrupts to notify the host software of card state changes. The controller uses this detection mechanism to manage power states, initialize communication protocols, and handle card hot-swap scenarios in compliance with the SD Host Standard specification.

features.name: Write Protection
features.description:
# Write Protection Feature (F_WRITE_PROTECT)

The Write Protection feature enables the SD Host Controller to detect and respect the write-protect status of inserted SD cards, preventing inadvertent data modification to protected media. This feature monitors the card's write-protect pin/switch and enforces write restrictions at the host controller level by blocking write commands when protection is active. The write-protect status is typically exposed through the Present State Register (Offset 024h) and works in conjunction with card detection to provide comprehensive card management and data integrity protection.

features.name: Timeout Control
features.description:
# Timeout Control (F_TIMEOUT)

**Purpose:** Timeout Control manages command and data transfer timeout mechanisms in the SD Host Controller, preventing the controller from indefinitely waiting for SD card responses or data completion. This feature monitors elapsed time during command execution and data transactions, automatically generating timeout interrupts or errors when predefined timeout thresholds are exceeded.

**Behavior:** The controller implements programmable timeout counters that are decremented based on the SDCLK frequency, with timeout values typically configured through dedicated timeout control registers. When a timeout condition is detected—such as a command not receiving a response or data transfer stalling—the controller halts the operation, sets appropriate status flags, and triggers an interrupt to notify the software, ensuring robust error handling and preventing system hangs during SD card communication failures.

features.name: Error Handling
features.description:
# Error Handling Feature

The Error Handling feature provides comprehensive detection, reporting, and management of errors that occur during SD Host Controller operations, including command execution failures, data transfer errors, and timeout conditions. This feature monitors various error conditions across command processing, DMA operations, and data transactions, capturing error status in dedicated interrupt and error status registers that signal the host software to take corrective action. The error handling mechanism works in conjunction with the interrupt control system to enable robust recovery procedures and ensure reliable SD card communication through proper error classification and reporting.

features.name: Software Reset
features.description:
# Software Reset Feature

The Software Reset feature provides a mechanism for the SD Host Controller driver to perform controlled resets of specific controller subsystems or the entire controller via register writes. This feature allows software to recover from error conditions, reinitialize the controller state, and clear internal state machines without requiring a full hardware power cycle. The reset operation is typically controlled through dedicated reset bits in the Host Control register, enabling selective reset of the command path, data path, or complete controller functionality.

features.name: Block Gap Control
features.description:
# Block Gap Control Feature

The Block Gap Control feature enables the SD Host Controller to pause and resume multi-block data transfers at block boundaries, allowing the host to insert gaps between blocks for priority operations or buffer management. This is implemented through the Block Gap Control Register (Offset 02Ah) and works in conjunction with the Suspend and Resume Mechanism (section 1.6) to gracefully halt ongoing transfers without corrupting data. The feature supports both read and write operations, enabling the controller to stop after the current block completes and resume from the next block when signaled by the host software.

features.name: Read Wait
features.description:
# Read Wait Feature (F_READ_WAIT)

The Read Wait feature enables the SD Host Controller to pause ongoing read data transfers from an SDIO card by asserting the READ_WAIT signal, allowing the host to manage buffer flow and prevent data overrun conditions. This mechanism is particularly useful in SDIO operations where the host needs to temporarily suspend data reception while maintaining the card's read state, enabling resumption without re-issuing commands. The feature is controlled through the Block Gap Control Register and works in conjunction with the block gap interrupt mechanism to provide seamless data flow management during multi-block read operations.

features.name: Suspend Resume
features.description:
# Suspend Resume Feature

The Suspend Resume feature enables the SD Host Controller to temporarily halt ongoing data transfers at block boundaries and subsequently resume them without losing data integrity or connection state. This mechanism is controlled through the Block Gap Control Register and allows the host to interrupt multi-block read/write operations to service higher-priority tasks or manage power states. The controller maintains the current transfer context and can seamlessly resume the suspended operation from the exact point of interruption, ensuring reliable data transactions in time-sensitive or power-constrained applications.

features.name: Wakeup Control
features.description:
# Wakeup Control Feature (F_WAKEUP)

The Wakeup Control feature enables the SD Host Controller to generate system wakeup events in response to specific SD card activities while the host system is in a low-power or suspended state. This feature allows the controller to selectively assert wakeup signals based on configured conditions such as card insertion/removal, card interrupt, or read-ready events, facilitating efficient power management without requiring continuous polling. The Wakeup Control Register (offset 02Ah area) provides software with the ability to enable/disable wakeup sources and configure which SD events should trigger system wake transitions.

features.name: Card Interrupt
features.description:
# Card Interrupt (F_CARD_INTERRUPT)

The Card Interrupt feature enables the SD Host Controller to detect and handle interrupt signals generated by SDIO cards, allowing asynchronous communication between the card and the host without polling. When an SDIO card asserts its interrupt line, the controller captures this event and can generate a host interrupt to notify the software, with interrupt enable/disable control managed through the interrupt control registers (as defined in section 1.8). This is essential for SDIO devices that require real-time event notification, such as WiFi adapters or other peripheral cards that need to signal the host of asynchronous events.

features.name: Capabilities
features.description:
# Capabilities Feature (F_CAPABILITIES)

The Capabilities feature defines and exposes the SD Host Controller's supported functionality and hardware capabilities through dedicated capability registers. This feature allows software to query what features the controller implements, such as DMA support types (SDMA/ADMA2), maximum clock frequencies, voltage support, and advanced features like Auto CMD12 or sampling clock tuning. By reading capability registers, drivers can dynamically adapt their operation to match the specific hardware capabilities rather than making assumptions, ensuring compatibility across different SD Host Controller implementations.

features.name: Preset Values
features.description:
# Preset Values Feature

**Purpose:** The Preset Values feature provides pre-configured register settings that optimize SD Host Controller performance for different SD bus speeds and operating modes, eliminating the need for manual tuning of clock dividers, drive strengths, and sampling delays.

**Behavior:** This capability-level feature stores multiple preset configurations in dedicated registers that can be automatically selected or manually applied based on the current SD speed mode (Normal, High, SDR12/25/50, DDR50, etc.), streamlining initialization and mode switching while ensuring compliance with SD specification timing requirements. The host controller can reference these preset values during clock tuning operations and mode transitions to quickly establish optimal electrical and timing parameters without firmware intervention.

features.name: Host Controller Version
features.description:
# Host Controller Version (F_HC_VERSION)

The Host Controller Version feature identifies the specification version and implementation level of the SD Host Controller, enabling software to determine which features and register sets are supported. This read-only capability register allows drivers to query the controller's compliance level with the SD Host Controller Standard and adapt their initialization and operation accordingly. It is essential for software compatibility and feature negotiation, particularly when supporting multiple controller implementations or versions.

features.name: Force Event
features.description:
# Force Event Feature (F_FORCE_EVENT)

The Force Event feature enables software to manually inject interrupt events into the SD Host Controller for testing and diagnostic purposes, bypassing normal hardware-triggered conditions. This configuration feature allows the host driver to simulate error conditions, status changes, or other interrupt events by directly writing to force event registers, facilitating validation of interrupt handling logic and error recovery mechanisms without requiring actual SD card state changes. It is typically used during development, debugging, and compliance testing to verify that the host controller's interrupt service routines respond correctly to various event scenarios.

features.name: Multiple Slot Support
features.description:
# Multiple Slot Support (F_MULTI_SLOT)

**Purpose:** This feature enables an SD Host Controller to manage and communicate with multiple SD/SDIO card slots simultaneously, allowing a single controller instance to handle independent card operations across different physical slots.

**Behavior:** When supported, the controller maintains separate command/response paths, data buffers, and interrupt handling for each slot, with register addressing or slot selection mechanisms that allow the host driver to target specific slots for command issuance, data transfer, and status monitoring. This capability is particularly useful in multi-card systems where independent card detection, initialization, and data transactions must occur without interference between slots.

**Note:** This feature is marked as NOT_SUPPORTED in your implementation, indicating the controller is designed for single-slot operation only.

features.name: Shared Bus Control
features.description:
# Shared Bus Control (F_SHARED_BUS)

Shared Bus Control enables multiple SD Host Controller slots to share a common SD bus interface, allowing sequential or arbitrated access to a single SD card by multiple host controller instances. This feature is part of the multi-slot support architecture and requires coordination between slots to manage command/response arbitration and data line multiplexing. Since this feature is marked as NOT_SUPPORTED, the host controller implementation does not provide hardware-level bus arbitration or sharing mechanisms, requiring software to manage multi-slot access through exclusive slot selection.

features.name: PME Wakeup
features.description:
# PME Wakeup Feature Description

PME (Power Management Event) Wakeup enables the SD Host Controller to generate a Power Management Event signal that can wake the system from a low-power or suspended state when specific card events occur. This feature allows the host controller to assert a PME signal to the system's power management logic, triggering a transition from sleep or suspend modes back to active operation based on configured wakeup conditions.

When enabled, the PME Wakeup mechanism monitors card insertion, removal, or interrupt events and generates the appropriate PME signal to the system chipset, enabling wake-on-card functionality without requiring the host processor to remain fully powered. This is typically controlled through the Wakeup Control Register and works in conjunction with the Suspend and Resume Mechanism to provide low-power card detection capabilities.
